**Situation** – While leading the migration of our recommendation engine from an in‑house Python stack to a cloud‑native microservice architecture, we discovered that our text embeddings were generated by two different platforms: AWS SageMaker for user reviews and GCP Vertex AI for product descriptions. The inconsistent vector spaces caused a 12 % drop in cosine similarity accuracy.

**Task** – I had to unify the embedding pipeline so that both sources produced comparable vectors without compromising latency or cost, while keeping the system deployable on each cloud provider’s CI/CD tooling.

**Action** – First, I benchmarked several open‑source models (SentenceTransformers, BERT‑Base) and chose a distilled RoBERTa model because it offered 30 % fewer FLOPs. Next, I containerized the inference code with Docker and deployed it to both SageMaker endpoints and Vertex AI custom containers, ensuring identical CPU/GPU configurations. To handle platform‑specific authentication, I wrote a lightweight wrapper that pulls credentials from each provider’s secret manager at runtime. Finally, I added a validation step in our nightly pipeline: embedding pairs from both platforms are compared against a held‑out test set; any drift beyond 0.01 cosine distance triggers an alert.

**Result** – After the rollout, cross‑platform similarity scores stabilized within 0.002 of each other, boosting recommendation precision by 7 % and reducing inference costs by ~15 %. I learned that standardizing on a single model architecture and automating cross‑cloud validation is key to maintaining ML quality when juggling multiple cloud services.
